results.title: An applicable simple map negates its window

results.title: Action of a list of simple maps
results.caption: Definition

A list $[j_1, \dots, j_r]$ of natural numbers acts on a binary word $u$ of length $n$ by $u \mapsto \varphi_{j_r}(\cdots(\varphi_{j_1}(u))\cdots)$: the head of the list acts first, and the empty list acts as the identity.

results.title: Lists of simple maps acting completely

results.title: Motzkin discriminant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Motzkin discriminant is the formal power series $1 - 2X - 3X^2 \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$, the discriminant in the generating functions for the Motzkin triangle.

results.title: Square roots of the Motzkin discriminant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A formal power series $s \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ is a Motzkin square root when $s^2 = 1 - 2X - 3X^2$ and the constant coefficient of $s$ is $1$.

results.title: Canonical square root of the Motzkin discriminant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The canonical square root is the power series $s = \sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{1/2}{n} (-2X - 3X^2)^n \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$, obtained by substituting $-2X - 3X^2$ for $Y$ in the binomial series $(1 + Y)^{1/2} = \sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{1/2}{n} Y^n$.

results.title: Second component of the Motzkin Riordan pair
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s = \sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{1/2}{n} (-2X - 3X^2)^n \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ be the canonical square root of $1 - 2X - 3X^2$. The power series $h \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ has $n$-th coefficient $\frac{1}{2} [X^{n+1}] (1 - X - s)$ for every $n \ge 0$. Since $1 - X - s$ has constant coefficient $0$, this is the quotient $h = (1 - X - s)/(2X)$.

results.title: First component of the Motzkin Riordan pair
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s = \sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{1/2}{n} (-2X - 3X^2)^n \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ be the canonical square root of $1 - 2X - 3X^2$, which has constant coefficient $1$. The power series $g \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ is the multiplicative inverse $g = s^{-1}$ of $s$, that is, $g = 1/\sqrt{1 - 2X - 3X^2}$.

results.title: Motzkin Riordan pairs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Formal power series $g, h \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ form a Motzkin Riordan pair when there is a power series $s \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ with $s^2 = 1 - 2X - 3X^2$ and constant coefficient $1$ such that $g s = 1$ and $2 X h = 1 - X - s$.

results.title: Bundled Motzkin Riordan pairs
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A bundled Motzkin Riordan pair consists of formal power series $g, h \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ together with a proof that they form a Motzkin Riordan pair: there is $s \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ with $s^2 = 1 - 2X - 3X^2$ and constant coefficient $1$ such that $g s = 1$ and $2 X h = 1 - X - s$.

results.title: Entries of a Motzkin Riordan array
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a Motzkin Riordan pair $(g, h)$ and natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the $(n, k)$ entry is the rational number $[X^n]\, g h^k$, the coefficient of $X^n$ in the power series $g h^k \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$.

results.title: The canonical Motzkin Riordan pair
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ be the canonical square root of $1 - 2X - 3X^2$, given by the binomial series, which has constant coefficient $1$. The canonical Motzkin Riordan pair is $(g, h)$ with $g = s^{-1}$ and $h = (1 - X - s)/(2X)$, the Motzkin Riordan pair conditions being witnessed by $s$.

results.title: Motzkin triangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s$ be the square root of $1 - 2X - 3X^2$ in the ring of formal power series over $\mathbb{Q}$ with constant coefficient $1$, and let $g = 1/s$ and $h = (1 - X - s)/(2X)$. For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the $(n, k)$ entry of the Motzkin triangle (OEIS A094531) is the rational number given by the coefficient of $X^n$ in $g h^k$.

results.title: Initial rows of the Motzkin triangle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Writing $T(n, k)$ for the $(n, k)$ entry of the canonical Motzkin triangle, the rows $n = 0, 1, 2, 3$ (with $0 \le k \le n$) are $T(0, 0) = 1$; $T(1, 0) = T(1, 1) = 1$; $T(2, 0) = 3$, $T(2, 1) = 2$, $T(2, 2) = 1$; and $T(3, 0) = 7$, $T(3, 1) = 6$, $T(3, 2) = 3$, $T(3, 3) = 1$, matching OEIS A094531.

results.title: Channel name in the π-calculus
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A channel name: a free channel `const n`, or the `i`-th enclosing binder `var i`.

results.title: Processes of the π-calculus
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Processes of the π-calculus. `inp a p` binds variable `0` in `p`; `nu p` binds variable `0` in `p` as a fresh channel.

results.title: Lifting free de Bruijn indices of a π-calculus name
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Shift free variables at or above `cutoff` up by one, e.g. when pushing a process under a binder.

results.title: Lifting free de Bruijn indices of a π-calculus process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Shift free variables of a process, entering binders with an increased cutoff.

results.title: Substitution of a name into a π-calculus name
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Substitute the name `n` for the variable at `cutoff`: variables below the cutoff are bound by inner binders and untouched, the variable at the cutoff is replaced by `n`, and variables above shift down by one.

results.title: Substitution of a name into a π-calculus process at a cutoff
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Substitute the name `n` for the variable at `cutoff` in a process. Under a binder, `n` is lifted by one at cutoff `0` so it keeps referring to the same outer names: every free index of `n` refers to a binder above the substitution point, so all of them shift. Lifting at the current cutoff would leave indices below the cutoff captured by the new binder.

results.title: Substitution for the innermost bound variable of a process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Substitute the name `n` for the innermost bound variable of `p`.

results.title: Swapping adjacent de Bruijn indices in a name
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Swap the two de Bruijn indices `cutoff` and `cutoff + 1` in a name: the two binders at that depth exchange places.

results.title: Swapping adjacent binders throughout a process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Swap the two binders at depth `cutoff` throughout a process, incrementing the cutoff under binders.

results.title: Substitution leaves constant channels and the empty process unchanged
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Substitution leaves a process with no `var 0` untouched: a constant channel stays constant, and the empty process stays empty.

results.title: Structural congruence of π-calculus processes
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Structural congruence: `|` is commutative and associative with unit `nil`, `ν` extrudes over `|` (lifting the other side, which cannot mention the fresh name), restriction of `nil` is `nil`, nested restrictions commute (swapping the two bound indices), and replication unfolds.

results.title: Guarded-choice resolution in the π-calculus
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Guarded-choice resolution: discard sum branches to reach a guarded process. Transitivity handles nested sums.

results.title: Reduction relation of the π-calculus
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Reduction: communication (substituting the sent channel for the input variable) between any selected output and input guards, reduction under `|` and `ν`, and reduction up to structural congruence.

results.title: IMP program states
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A state of an IMP program is a function $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ assigning a natural-number value $\sigma(i)$ to each variable, where variables are identified by natural numbers $i$.

results.title: Arithmetic expressions of IMP
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The arithmetic expressions of IMP are built inductively from the constants $n$, one for each natural number $n$, and the variables $x_i$, one for each natural number $i$: if $a_1$ and $a_2$ are arithmetic expressions, then so are $a_1 + a_2$, $a_1 - a_2$ and $a_1 \cdot a_2$.

results.title: Boolean expressions of IMP
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The Boolean expressions of IMP are built inductively from the constants true and false and the comparisons $a_1 = a_2$ and $a_1 \le a_2$ of arithmetic expressions $a_1, a_2$: if $b$, $b_1$ and $b_2$ are Boolean expressions, then so are the negation $\neg b$ and the conjunction $b_1 \wedge b_2$.

results.title: Commands of IMP
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The commands of the while-language IMP are built inductively from skip and the assignments $x_i := a$ of an arithmetic expression $a$ to the variable $x_i$ with index $i \in \mathbb{N}$: if $c$, $c_1$ and $c_2$ are commands and $b$ is a Boolean expression, then so are the sequential composition $c_1 ; c_2$, the conditional if $b$ then $c_1$ else $c_2$, and the loop while $b$ do $c$.

results.summary: The big-step relation says when running a command $c$ from a state $s$ terminates in a state $t$; we then say that $c$ takes $s$ to $t$. It is the least relation satisfying the following rules. The command $\mathtt{skip}$ takes $s$ to $s$. results.title: Determinism of IMP big-step semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every command $c$ and every state $s$, if $c$ run from $s$ terminates in a state $t_1$ and also in a state $t_2$ under the big-step semantics, then $t_1 = t_2$.

results.title: IMP configuration
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A configuration of IMP is a pair $(c, \sigma)$ of a command $c$ and a state $\sigma$.

results.title: IMP small-step relation
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The single-step relation $\to$ on IMP configurations is the smallest relation satisfying the following rules, for all variables $x$, arithmetic expressions $a$, Boolean expressions $b$, commands $c, c_1, c_1', c_2$ and states $\sigma, \sigma'$. Assignment: $(x := a, \sigma) \to (\mathtt{skip}, \sigma[x \mapsto v])$, where $v$ is the value of $a$ in $\sigma$. Sequencing:…

results.title: IMP multi-step relation
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The relation $\to^*$ on IMP configurations is the reflexive, transitive closure of the small-step relation: $x \to^* y$ when $y$ is reached from $x$ by a finite sequence of zero or more small steps.

results.title: Termination of an IMP command
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A command $c$ terminates from an initial state $\sigma$ in a final state $\tau$ when the configuration $(c, \sigma)$ reaches $(\mathtt{skip}, \tau)$ in finitely many small steps.

results.title: Determinism of IMP small-step semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all IMP configurations $x$, $y$, $z$, if $x$ steps to $y$ and $x$ steps to $z$ in one small step, then $y = z$.

results.title: Big-step executions terminate in small steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and states $s$ and $s'$, if $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics, then $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s'$: finitely many small steps lead from the configuration $(c, s)$ to $(\mathrm{skip}, s')$.

results.title: Prepending one small step to a big-step execution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x = (c, s)$ and $y = (d, t)$ be configurations and $s'$ a state. If $x$ moves to $y$ in one small step and $d$ evaluates from $t$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics, then $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics.

results.title: Prepending finitely many small steps to a big-step execution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x = (c, s)$ and $y = (d, t)$ be configurations and $s'$ a state. If $x$ reaches $y$ in finitely many (possibly zero) small steps and $d$ evaluates from $t$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics, then $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics.

results.title: Small-step termination implies big-step evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and states $s$ and $s'$, if $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s'$, then $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics.

results.title: Equivalence of small-step and big-step semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and states $s$ and $s'$, $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s'$ if and only if $c$ evaluates from $s$ to $s'$ in the big-step semantics.

results.title: Small-step termination is deterministic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every IMP command $c$ and states $s$, $s_1$, $s_2$, if $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s_1$ and also terminates by small steps in $s_2$, then $s_1 = s_2$.

results.title: Hoare validity via small-step termination
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For assertions $P$ and $Q$ on states and an IMP command $c$, the partial-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid if and only if, for all states $s$ and $s'$, whenever $P$ holds in $s$ and $c$ started in $s$ terminates by small steps in $s'$, $Q$ holds in $s'$.

results.title: Number of permutations with a given cycle type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of permutations of `n` letters with cycle type `π`, `w(π) = n! / ∏ j, j ^ (a j) * (a j)!` with `a j = π.parts.count j` (Cauchy's formula).

results.title: Probability of a given number of alleles under the Ewens formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The probability `P_θ(K = k)` that a sample of `n` genes carries exactly `k` distinct alleles under the Ewens sampling formula.

results.title: Ewens conditional probability given the number of alleles
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conditional probability of the allelic partition `π` given that the number of alleles is `K = K(π) = π.parts.card`, under the Ewens sampling formula with parameter `θ`.

results.title: Conditional upper-tail p-value of the Ewens–Watterson test
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conditional upper-tail p-value of a statistic `T` of the allelic partition: the conditional probability, given the observed number of alleles `K(π)`, that `T` is at least its observed value `T π`. It is written with the cycle-type weights and so does not involve `θ` (by `ewensCondProb_eq` it is the conditional tail probability for every `θ > 0`).

results.title: Sample homozygosity of an allelic partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The sample homozygosity `F(π) = ∑_i (n_i / n)²`, the sum over the alleles of the squared sample frequencies (Watterson 1978); `n_i` ranges over the parts of `π`.

results.title: Positivity of the cycle-type weight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The cycle-type weight is positive.

results.title: Factorization of the Ewens sampling formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Factorization of the Ewens sampling formula (Ewens 1972): `P_θ(π) = θ ^ K(π) / θ^{(n)} * w(π)`, with `K(π) = π.parts.card` the number of alleles.

results.title: `K` is sufficient for `θ`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `K` is sufficient for `θ` (Ewens 1972): for `θ > 0`, the conditional law of the allelic partition given the number of alleles is `w(π) / ∑_{K(π') = K(π)} w(π')`, which does not depend on `θ`.

results.title: Cauchy's count by number of cycles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The cycle-type weights of the partitions of `n` into `k` parts sum to the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind `|s(n, k)|`.

results.title: Law of the number of alleles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Law of the number of alleles (Ewens 1972): `P_θ(K = k) = |s(n, k)| θ ^ k / θ^{(n)}`. As an identity between the defining sums it holds for every real `θ`; it is a probability for `θ > 0`.

results.title: The Ewens–Watterson conditional law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Ewens–Watterson conditional law (Ewens 1972; Watterson 1978): for `θ > 0`, `P(π | K = K(π)) = w(π) / |s(n, K(π))| = n! / (|s(n, k)| ∏ j, j ^ (a j) (a j)!)`.

results.title: Validity of a discrete upper-tail p-value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For nonnegative masses `q` on a finite set `s` and a statistic `T`, the upper-tail p-value `p x = ∑_{y ∈ s, T x ≤ T y} q y` satisfies `∑_{x ∈ s, p x ≤ t} q x ≤ t` for every `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: Conditional validity of the Ewens–Watterson test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `θ > 0`, every number of alleles `k` and every level `t ≥ 0`, the conditional probability given `K = k` that the conditional upper-tail p-value of `T` is at most `t` is at most `t`.

results.title: Validity of the Ewens–Watterson test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Validity of the Ewens–Watterson test (Watterson 1978): for every `θ > 0` and every level `t ≥ 0`, the Ewens probability that the conditional upper-tail p-value of `T` is at most `t` is at most `t`. With `T = homozygosity` this is the test against excess homozygosity, with `T = -homozygosity` the test against a deficit of homozygosity.
